idea-plugin.name: Bun Console
idea-plugin.description:
Interactive console (REPL) for JavaScript and TypeScript code of your project, running on Bun: a playground where the code you are editing is ready to call.

  • Call your code directly. Functions, classes and variables of the file open in the editor are available by name, exported or not, with no imports.
  • Debug from the console. Breakpoints stop console calls; while any JavaScript program you debug is paused, the console evaluates in the selected stack frame.
  • Iterate freely. Variables persist between commands, and const, let and class can be declared again as you refine a snippet.
  • Run a file or a selection. One click runs the whole file in the editor, or the code you selected (TypeScript too), in the console.
  • Safe by default. Switching editor tabs never runs code: a file runs only when the console first uses it or you run it. Uncaught errors are printed, never fatal.

Also: top-level await that never blocks the console, import statements, highlighting, completion of runtime names, command history, and more files in context with Add File to Bun Console or Add Symbol to Bun Console. If you use the browser developer console, it will feel familiar.

Works in WebStorm and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate. Requires Bun 1.4 or newer; the debugger also needs the Bun plugin (bundled with WebStorm). Open View | Tool Windows | Bun Console. Documentation: bunconsole.dev
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.4

  • Run File: runs the whole file in the editor again and shows its output; Run Selection: runs the selected code as console input, TypeScript included, and asks before running a file whose names it needs. Both are buttons in the console's title bar and commands in the editor's context menu; the title bar buttons stay visible while you work in the editor.
  • Scroll to the End and Clear Output buttons in the console's title bar.
  • Find Action (Ctrl+Shift+A) finds the console as "JavaScript Console", "TypeScript Console" or "REPL".
  • Works in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate: the Bun plugin is no longer required; only the debugger needs it, and the console explains how to get it.
  • Finding Bun on PATH no longer uses an IDE API scheduled for removal (compatible with WebStorm 2026.3).

0.2.3

  • Dynamic import() in the console resolves relative paths from the context file, like static imports; import('b.ts') suggests './b.ts'.
  • Module namespaces print as Module { … }.

0.2.2

  • The console does nothing until you use it: a tool window restored with the project no longer starts Bun; it starts on the first click into the input, command or console action.
  • While the tool window is hidden, the console does not follow the editor; it catches up when shown.
  • No false "Unavailable until Restart Runtime" message for names added to a file after it was loaded.

0.2.1

  • Fixed an IDE error ("There is no ProgressIndicator or Job in this thread") when the console restored its context in TypeScript projects, even before the console was used.
  • Add Symbol to Bun Console resolves the symbol in the background instead of on the UI thread.
  • Long arrays of numbers and strings use the full console width; values are never cut short.
  • console.clear() clears the console; running a command scrolls to the end.
  • Editing a file with breakpoints no longer restarts the runtime while you type.

0.2.0

  • Evaluates in the paused frame of any JavaScript program you debug.
  • Console output appears in order with command results.
  • Context files are no longer executed when you switch editor tabs.
  • Non-exported top-level declarations are available by name.
  • Awaited commands no longer block the console; a busy JavaScript thread is reported.
  • Uncaught errors no longer stop the runtime; console and project code share one realm.
  • Debugger toggle in the tool window; Restart also ends processes started from the console.
